core_claims.name: LE / lePred / leZero / leRefl / leTrans / leAntisym / leTotal
core_claims.scope: Unbounded inductive natural non-strict ordering, inversion, zero characterization, reflexivity, transitivity, antisymmetry, and comparability for every pair of naturals.

core_claims.name: addMono / mulMono
core_claims.scope: Both addition and multiplication are monotone in both arguments under independent LE premises, for arbitrary naturals.

core_claims.name: LT / ltTrans / ltToLe / ltIrreflexive / ltAddMono / trichotomy
core_claims.scope: Strict order is LE(S m,n), with transitivity, conversion to non-strict order, irreflexivity, strict two-argument addition monotonicity, and trichotomy.

core_claims.name: Even / Odd / evenPlusEven / oddPlusEven / evenPlusOdd / oddPlusOdd
core_claims.scope: Mutually inductive parity evidence and all four parity-of-addition combinations, proved by mutual structural recursion.

core_claims.name: One / Canonical / canonicalInc / canonicalTo
core_claims.scope: Leading-one and canonical raw binary predicates; increment preserves canonicality; every natural encoding is canonical.

core_claims.name: onePositive / toDoublePositive / toDouble / oneRoundTrip / canonicalRoundTrip
core_claims.scope: Leading-one evidence implies positive value. Encoding doubling commutes with appending zero under a positive-value premise. Encoding a decoded canonical bitstring returns that bitstring.

core_claims.name: oneUnique / canonicalUnique
core_claims.scope: For any fixed raw bitstring, any two One proofs are equal and any two Canonical proofs are equal; no general proof irrelevance is assumed.

deviations: LT is represented definitionally as LE(S m,n), instead of a separate but equivalent inductive strict-order datatype. The successor/non-strict correspondence is therefore definitional.
Multiple presentation variants of totality and transitivity are consolidated into single general proofs.
